- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, reduce peak values by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., price drops after recent high), model often fails to reflect this; dampen forecast slope toward prior mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates in high-sentiment periods; add 2–5% bias upward if sentiment > 0.7.
- If sentiment turns sharply negative after a spike, model often fails to anticipate reversal; add early downward correction.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67), model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted to align with recent 5–7 day moving average.
